title: Down Screen and Curl
description: A player sets a down screen for a teammate who curls hard off it toward the rim, learning to read when to curl versus pop.

content.objective: Set a solid down screen, then read whether to curl, pop or fade off it.
content.setup: A screener sets up at the elbow; a cutter starts at the block.
instructions: The screener sets a wide, stationary screen at the elbow.
The cutter comes off the screen tight, brushing the screener's shoulder.
If the defender trails, the cutter curls directly to the rim.
If the defender goes under, the cutter pops out to the wing for a catch-and-shoot instead.
coachingPoints: The screener must be set and stationary before contact, not moving into it.
The cutter should read the defender's path, not guess.
Change speed off the screen to create real separation.
commonMistakes: Screener moving into the defender instead of staying set.
Cutter drifting too far from the screen, giving the defender room to recover.
Cutting without actually drawing any real defensive attention.
content.safety: The screener holds a legal, stationary position — no moving into contact.
